searchText: Back from vacation, immediately with my first question: Stumped why this test should pass, code `6000e0000000` seems to have some unreachable code to me (three STOP instructions in a row ``` ./eofdump eofdump -hex 0xef00010100040200010006030001001404000000008000016000e0000000ef000101000402000100010400000000800000fe Header ----------- EOFMagic: ef00 EOFVersion: 01 KindType: 01 TypesSize: 0004 KindCode: 02 CodeSize: 0001 Code 0 length: 0006 KindContainer: 03 ContainerSize: 0001 Container 0 length: 0014 KindData: 04 DataSize: 0000 Terminator: 00 ----------- Body ----------- Type 0: 00800001 Code 0: 6000e0000000 Section 0: ef000101000402000100010400000000800000fe Data: ``` The `e0` is `RJUMP` followed by 2 bytes of immediate value. Then you have single `STOP`. I forgot rjump takes immediates... That's one reason I wrote a pretty printer. I always look at my validation errors in pretty printed code.
